recall.question: B4: Write single-head self-attention.
recall.answer: p_{t,j} = softmax(q_t k_j^T / sqrt(d_h)), h^out_t = sum_j p_{t,j} v_j.

recall.question: B6: State the causal mask.
recall.answer: M_{t,j} = 0 for j <= t, -infinity for j > t, added before the softmax. Guarantees position t depends only on current and past tokens.

keyTerms.definition: Per-head compute and KV-cache memory for prefill and decode.
MHA 128.0 MiB, GQA 32.0 MiB, MQA 4.0 MiB per layer at T = 8192.
The cache stores one K/V head per group: n_g groups.

recall.question: D2.2: Report the KV cache table.
recall.answer: Per layer at T = 8192 fp16: MHA 128.0 MiB, GQA (n_g = 8) 32.0 MiB, MQA 4.0 MiB.

recall.question: D2.3: Why does the GQA cache scale with n_g?
recall.answer: The cache stores one K/V head per group, and there are n_g groups; query heads share within a group.

keyTerms.definition: Row t of softmax_row(Q K^T / c + M) equals the score vector of (17.23).
Softmax at tau = 0.5, 1.0, 2.0; top-p and top-k renormalized.

recall.question: Q1: Show the masked row identity.
recall.answer: Row t of Q K^T / c holds q_t k_j^T / c. The causal mask sets j > t to -infinity; softmax_row gives exactly 0 for j > t: the vector of (17.23).

keyTerms.definition: Append k_new/v_new before computing scores.
One query vs n_h query heads under GQA.

recall.question: T1: Identify the two KV-cache bugs.
recall.answer: Bug 1: the new key/value are appended after the attention computation, so each token never attends to its own position. Bug 2: the code assumes one key head; under GQA the query has n_h heads.

keyTerms.definition: GQA/MQA or sliding window (quality cost); cache accounting with eviction (latency cost).
Loss falls while answers do not improve; flip the loss mask.

recall.question: S1: How do you serve 128k context on 40 GB?
recall.answer: Architectural: switch MHA to GQA/MQA or add sliding-window attention. Systems: per-sequence cache accounting with eviction/offload. Measure quality at 128k before shipping.

recall.question: S2: What are the symptoms of an inverted loss mask?
recall.answer: Symptoms: the loss mainly predicts prompt tokens so it falls while answer quality does not improve; generations parrot prompt-like text. Fix: flip the loss mask.

keyTerms.definition: Zero-shot scores depend on exact prompt wording.
Same prompts for both models; report mean and spread across variants.

recall.question: R1: Critique the zero-shot claim.
recall.answer: Confound: zero-shot scores depend on the exact prompt wording. Protocol: fix a prompt set before seeing results, evaluate both models on the same prompts, report mean and spread across variants.
